summary: Astronaut Mission Trainer is an educational Mars-outpost simulation that turns space science into an engaging decision-making experience. Players manage power, life support, food production, radiation shielding, and communications while responding to realistic challenges such as solar flares, dust storms, and Earth–Mars communication delays. The project addresses the challenge by making the engineering trade-offs of running a lunar or Martian outpost tangible and interactive for students. It combines NASA and JPL data, historical mission scenarios, multiplayer communication, and a 3D diorama-style interface. After each mission, players receive a debrief explaining the causes and consequences of their decisions, helping them build systems-thinking, problem-solving, and space-science skills.
details:
Asteria is an educational Mars-outpost simulation that helps students learn how astronauts make decisions in space. Players manage power, life support, food, radiation shielding, and communication while responding to real-world conditions such as solar flares, dust storms, Earth–Mars communication delays, and solar conjunctions. The project combines NASA and JPL data with historical mission scenarios and a black-box investigation of failed missions. We developed it using TypeScript, React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, Node.js, Express, Socket.IO, PostgreSQL, Prisma, and Three.js with React Three Fiber. The project is creative because it turns real space science into an interactive 3D game where every decision has consequences, then provides a debrief explaining what happened and what the player can learn. Our team considered accessibility for students, performance on school devices, offline fallbacks, multiplayer communication delays, data accuracy, privacy, and youth safety.
Super Intelligence tools, including ChatGPT/Claude, were used to assist with software development, documentation, brainstorming, and refining educational content. The team reviewed, tested, and adapted all generated material. NASA and other source data were independently selected and cited by the team. No SI-generated images, video, or audio were used unless explicitly labeled.
